claims.text: A high-throughput DFT-based approach can accurately determine melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
A high-throughput DFT-based approach can accurately determine enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A high-throughput DFT-based approach can accurately determine entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A high-throughput DFT-based approach can accurately determine volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
A high-throughput DFT-based approach can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed DFT-based approach will determine these thermodynamic properties efficiently.
The proposed approach is applicable across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Chemical short-range order is the structural mediator relevant to the proposed thermodynamic-property calculations.
Relative to a random alloy, the proposed intervention will increase lattice heat conductivity by 12% across high-entropy alloys.
The accuracy of the DFT-based approach may depend on the particular high-entropy-alloy composition.
The accuracy of the DFT-based approach may depend on input-data quality.
The approach can be validated by comparing predicted and experimental thermodynamic properties for a range of high-entropy alloys.
A deviation of more than 10% between predicted and experimental values falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis concerns prediction of melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties, whereas the stated predicted outcome is a change in solid-state lattice heat conductivity.

The proposed phonon-scattering mechanism does not coherently explain the claimed conductivity increase. The cited record says scattering by SRO precipitates would conventionally be expected to decrease conductivity and instead attributes the observed increase to SRO-cluster percolation pathways.
